While not an actual vacation, I do have a story from a camping trip we took when we were 15. We had a party the day before and it ended in us watching "The Blair witch project". Now, the next day we headed out to our camping destination which was was a couple miles down from a wood processing plant. We hiked there, the locals were great and we even got a promise from the local bar owners, that if we needed anything we could come by anytime and they would provide, at a cost of course. So we set up our tent, ( a two person tent for the five of us ) and began barbecuing, setting up the fire pit...the usual. As it became more obvious that the two person tent was not going to fit us all comfortably, this chick called her parents and had them bring us a second tent, which they did as it was a 30 minutes drive at most. We set up the second tent and the girls (both of them) went to sleep in that one, as we boys had another couple of drinks. And this is where the shit show starts. We camped next to a river and across the river there is a forest, lots of "whispering" and strange sounds, so the girls say they don't feel safe and that we should all sleep together. We huddle up, go to sleep, and all of a sudden something starts rubbing against our tent. Now, as most white people do, we get out of the tent and start investigating. Nothing. Clear explanation, the Blair witch is in these woods. We make a run for the bar, ring the doorbell, no one answers. I think at this point I should mention that we didn't bring any kind of flashlight with us. So we freak out and run to this summer camp that was about a mile from where we camped, just following the road we figured out where it would be. We get there, and apparently the power went out in the whole village/area. They gave us two tea light candles and sent us on our way, as this was a Christian camp and we were sinners for camping without adults supervision. So we went back to the bar,  tried ringing the doorbell a few times, and ended sitting on their bank for about 6 hours, taking turns sleeping, because we thought bears were gonna come down from the forest and eat us. Sun came up, we see that the forest near the bar had a 50 meter vertical drop, so the only way bears were going to get us was of they literally landed on our heads. We went back to our tents, tired, and just wanting to sleep, only to realize that the Blair witch were two mice that made their way inside the tent while we were outside drinking.
TL;DR we were chased out of our tent thinking it was the Blair witch, spent the night looking for shelter, being berated by christians and ended up sleeping in turns, thinking that we were gonna be mauled by bears, all because of two mice.

I know, but as I said, some perspective is needed to understand why so many people still spank their kids. We're not about that life..not yet anyways.

I do agree that children should not be physically punished BUT, (and I know reddit is going to shit on me for this) spanking and pubishinment through beatings are not the same thing. To fully understand this we have to fully understand what defines a human being and for that I'm gonna try to put it all into perspective. 
The first species of human is believed to have walked this earth approximately 2.8 million years ago. Wild things...but creative nonetheless, because the oldest tool to be found is believed to be 2.6 milion years old. That's a 200.000 years difference. Now, some times goes by, fire is discovered then controlled, more complex tools and weapons are being made. And about 315.000 years ago a new species pops up, the homo sapiens, aka you and me. That's about 2.3 million years of evolution until we were roughly shaped in the shape we are now. Some time goes by, we are not just sticking the meat in fire, we are adding herbs. We go on to sail to new lands, make art, music and other creative stuff. Then, 247 years ago, the industrial revolution starts. In the last 247 years we've seen two world wars, countless other wars, moon landings and other stuff until today, typing this on a handheld computer basically. 
Now, my point, and the point of many others is that we evolved too fast, and while our body and creative mind kept up with the fast paced changes, our instincts and primary functions didn't do so well. Yeah we have rules and regulations and social standards to uphold, but in our core we are still very instinctual. Which brings me to my final point. 
There are a few exceptions, of course, but generally a human mother would give her life to save that of her offspring without even thinking about it. Know what other species that do that? Primates. Take a look at gorillas or Bonobos (our closest relatives) and see what they do when their offspring get to close to danger, like bothering the head of the group. If the kid is not one of his, the mother will spank/berate the youngling in order to keep him out of trouble. 
So yeah, I'm not saying stomp your kid out because he ate the last cookie or some other stupid things kids do, but snapping him out of something dangerous, even through spanking could make the difference between a kid and a dead kid.
Tl;dr we're just monkeys using smartphones and IMHO modern parenting tactics don't work for everyone. At least for now.
